title: Working on my first vibe-coded game and I'm still mindblown at what Claude is capable of doing.
author: ArkhamDreamerZero
selftext:
I've been a film director for years, but video games have always been a huge passion of mine. Recently, I decided to see what happens when you try "vibe-coding" a game with Claude... and I'm honestly mind-blown.

When I started, the first output was far from perfect. It was pretty ugly, kind of boring, and lasted about 5 minutes. But the fact that it was actually playable from a single prompt was shocking.

The real magic happened when I realized I didn't have to stop there. Once I started doing non-stop back-and-forth prompts, feeding it visual inspirations, tweaking level design, adjusting mechanics, and directing the narrative, it became clear I could turn this into a full project.

Fast forward to now, and I've expanded the playtime to around 30 minutes, layered in a full-fledged story, and made the whole thing genuinely scary and actually fun to play. All the code and logic were built entirely in Claude, while the sprites were generated and refined with ChatGPT.

It's still far from finished, but I'm having an absolute blast directing a game the same way I'd direct a film. Check out the clip above, and let me know your thoughts, feedback, or questions about the process!

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body: not bad op but buddy still runs like he is trying to get caught

replies.author: ArkhamDreamerZero
replies.body: I can see that haha! The whole game takes place inside a house though, so that's why I don't want to bump up the speed tooooo much. Do you have any suggestion? Context: The game is mostly hide and seek. Meaning the stalker enemy will emit a warning before appearing, so you have like 5-9 seconds to hide. So you're not actually running away from the creature most of the time.

replies.author: drahgon
replies.body: Yeah, you could probably ask Claude to just iterate on the running and make it look more realistic but to be honest with that art style. I don’t think it’s the biggest deal.

replies.author: ArkhamDreamerZero
replies.body: Yeah I've done SOOO many iterations haha! Right now I'm more focused on the creature, but I'll come back to the main character at some point.

replies.author: drahgon
replies.body: Yeah, in my game I have a mechanics critic that has to give the sign off on things like this, and then a quality audit credit that gives the Final say on the entire game quality. So often times you know they’ll self loop for several iterations, and I find that it usually ends up with something really good.

comments.author: drahgon
comments.body: I just wanted to say I really really love the art style!

replies.author: ArkhamDreamerZero
replies.body: Thanks! I've been on a retro game kick recently, like The Pactmaker, Dreams in the Witch House, things like that. That's what I was aiming for, but I'm still looking for ways to improve.

comments.author: Guildbound
comments.body: Depending on how you made your art/assets Claude is beast at making its own tools inside of Claude I was getting bad animations and don’t know how I made a rigging tool inside of Claude that I can tell it what part of the body to move

replies.body: Pretty sure Claude made a rigging system for my game too. Now body parts move independently. So I'll try to tweak with that in mind.
